tex_content.label: claim:ball-contained-in-horn-compact-closure
tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Balls around $x_n$ eventually lie in the horn with compact closure] For every $A<\infty $, eventually $B(x_n,0,AQ_n^{-1/2})$ lies in the $2\epsilon $-horn and has compact closure. \end{claim}
Proof

↗ bcbd\sketch Boundary points have curvature at most $16C^2\rho ^{-2}$ and their necks control curvature by $32C^2\rho ^{-2}$ within distance $\epsilon ^{-1}\rho /2C$. Hence the rescaled distance to the boundary tends to infinity. Distance to the horn end also tends to infinity, since otherwise Theorem bcbd is violated.

□
